sections.h2: Is a quick sale realistic for an Easton house?
sections.html:
Yes. Easton owners can list with an agent, sell without one, or take an as-is cash purchase. The condition of the house, any tenants and your closing date usually decide which. Deferred repairs, a tenant lease or a clouded inheritance are the common reasons an owner here looks at cash.

Easton is the seat of Northampton County, at the eastern end of the Lehigh Valley where the Lehigh River meets the Delaware. Phillipsburg, New Jersey, sits across the river, so some buyers commute over the bridges. The population was 28,127 in 2020 and 30,402 in July 2025. Owners live in 44.5% of the city's homes, so a good share of the houses you compete with are rentals.

The typical owner's home is worth $196,300 for 2020 to 2024, against a typical household income of $69,348. Citywide medians blur big differences between a renovated Downtown block and an unrenovated College Hill one, so price your house against recent sales close to it.

The city has four districts: Downtown, College Hill, South Side and West Ward. Houses sit close together, and older ones often need a look at the roof, gutters and plumbing after a hard winter.

sections.h2: City offices that touch an Easton sale
sections.html:
Start with Code Enforcement, then the Historic District Commission, then the rental licensing desk if anyone rents the house. Code Enforcement applies the city Property Maintenance Code and the Pennsylvania Uniform Construction Code, and it can tell you whether permits on your address are still open.

  • Permits: building, enlarging, altering, repairing, moving or demolishing a structure, changing its use, or installing electrical, gas, mechanical or plumbing systems all need one.
  • Historic review: facade and signage work may also need a certificate of appropriateness from the Historic District Commission.
  • Occupancy cap: a single housekeeping unit may hold no more than three unrelated people, and an Occupancy Limitations Certificate states the limit for each dwelling unit.
  • Rental paperwork: an owner who rents files each tenant's name and address with the Rental Licensing Officer, and a moving permit comes from the Finance Department.
  • Fire check: the fire inspector will do a free fire safety inspection if you doubt a building has the required smoke detectors.

For a rented house, put the lease, rental license papers and tenant form in one folder. A buyer's attorney will ask for them.

Expect separate bills from the city, the county and the school district. Easton levies 24.95 mills on the value the Northampton County Assessment Office sets. Residents also pay a city earned income tax of 1.45% plus 0.5% to Easton Area School District, for 1.95% in all.

The county mailed 2026 bills in mid-January. The discount ended March 31, and the face amount was due June 1. Taxes still unpaid at the close of business on January 31 of the next year pass to the Tax Claim Bureau. Clear any balance from the sale proceeds.

The state realty transfer tax is 1% of value, and the law makes the grantor and the grantee jointly liable. The Recorder of Deeds, at (610) 829-6210, collects it with any local tax at recording, and the city's tax list includes a real estate transfer tax. Ask for the combined rate at your price before you sign a contract.

To appeal an assessment, call the Assessment Division on the second floor of the courthouse at 669 Washington Street for the current filing deadline. School homestead exclusions come from Act 72 of 2004, so an owner-occupant should ask the school district how the exclusion is handled when the deed changes.

sections.h2: What an Easton seller must tell the buyer
sections.html:
Anyone selling one to four dwelling units in Pennsylvania has to hand the buyer a written property statement under 68 Pa.C.S. section 7303. It must be filled in, signed and dated, and it is due ahead of the sales agreement. The state form runs through 16 topics, among them the roof, the basement, hazardous substances and title defects.

A seller who willfully or negligently falls short owes the buyer's actual damages, and a suit has to begin within two years after final settlement (section 7311). Executors and other fiduciaries selling for an estate fall outside the chapter (section 7302). A cash buyer does not change any of this.

sections.h2: How a cash sale runs from first call to closing
sections.html:
You contact the buyer with the address and the facts that affect value: condition, tenants, open permits or code notices, and who holds title. The buyer reviews that, then makes an offer for the house as it stands. If you accept, a title search begins, and any lien, unpaid tax or estate question surfaces at that stage.

Before closing, gather the deed, the latest city, county and school bills, any lease and rental license records, and payoff letters for loans. An heir or executor should also bring the estate attorney's paperwork. At the table you sign the deed and settlement papers, taxes or liens are paid from the proceeds, and the deed goes to the Recorder of Deeds. You hand over the keys when the funds clear, and you choose the date within what title work allows.

sections.h2: When cash is the better route
sections.html:
Cash fits best when condition, occupancy or timing would stall a listing. Typical Easton situations:

  • A house left by a relative that no heir wants to keep.
  • A rental where the unit or the license paperwork needs attention.
  • Open permits or code notices that scare off buyers who depend on a mortgage.
  • Roof, plumbing or heating damage after a hard winter.
  • A job transfer, divorce or court date that fixes your move.

A cash sale skips the loan underwriting, the buyer's appraisal and the repair negotiations that often follow an inspection. Title work and the closing date you pick set the pace. Compare any cash figure with what a listing would net after repairs, concessions and transfer tax. To get a figure for an Easton address, call or text with the details, including tenants and any open code items.

faqs.q: What controls the speed of a cash closing in Easton?
faqs.a: Title work and the date you choose control it, since there is no loan to underwrite. The deed then goes to the Northampton County Recorder of Deeds, and taxes or liens come out of the proceeds.

faqs.q: Who owes the Pennsylvania transfer tax in Easton?
faqs.a: Under state law both the person giving the deed and the person receiving it are liable for the 1% state tax. Your sales agreement decides how the cost is divided, and the Recorder of Deeds collects any local share with it.

faqs.q: Is a tenant a problem when selling in Easton?
faqs.a: No, but paperwork matters. Owners who rent keep tenant names and addresses on file with the Rental Licensing Officer, so give the buyer the lease and those records.

faqs.q: Where is a deed recorded for an Easton property?
faqs.a: At the Northampton County Recorder of Deeds, which records deeds and mortgages and collects the fees and taxes due on transfers. The office number is (610) 829-6210.

faqs.q: Can I sell an inherited Easton house?
faqs.a: Yes. Pennsylvania exempts property passed by will or intestate succession from realty transfer tax, and a fiduciary selling for an estate falls outside the seller disclosure chapter. Settle title questions with the estate's attorney before setting a closing date.
